cards.title: 46.1% of all customer signup attempts were malicious in 2024
cards.description: Across the Auth0 platform in 2024, the median daily proportion of registration attempts that met the criteria of a signup attack was 46.1% — reversing a prior downward trend and consistent with a surge in fraudulent signups reported across other large tech companies, attributed to AI-enabled attack workflows.
cards.comparison: reverses a prior downward trend; surge attributed to AI
cards.pageOrSection: Threats against customer identity — Signup attacks

cards.title: Peak day: 92.5% of signups were attack attempts
cards.description: On April 6, 2024, 92.5% of registration attempts on the Auth0 platform met the criteria of a signup attack. In contrast, the lowest day of the year (February 29) still saw 14.4% — a major outlier, as no other day fell below 30%.
cards.pageOrSection: Threats against customer identity — Signup attacks

cards.title: Retail/eCommerce and FinServ are the top targets for fake signups
cards.description: Median daily proportion of signup attempts that met the criteria of a signup attack in 2024, by industry. Retail/eCommerce led at nearly 70%, with Financial Services close behind at ~65%, well above the all-industries mean of 44.5%.
cards.comparison: vs. mean of per-industry daily medians (44.5%)
cards.pageOrSection: Fraudsters focus on retail and finance

cards.title: Enterprises absorb the most fake-signup traffic
cards.description: Median daily proportion of signup attempts meeting attack criteria, broken out by customer segment in 2024. Enterprises faced 64.3% — more than three times the rate seen by mid-market organizations.
cards.pageOrSection: Fraudsters focus on retail and finance

cards.title: 120x: attack signups outnumbered real signups during a sustained retail campaign
cards.description: During a multi-month sustained attack against the Retail/eCommerce sector — which endured the highest proportion of attack signups of any industry in 2024 — the number of signup-attack events exceeded the number of legitimate signups by a factor of 120.
cards.pageOrSection: The massive scale of signup attacks

cards.title: 16.9% of customer logins showed clear malicious behavior
cards.description: Across the Auth0 platform in 2024, the median daily proportion of login attempts that exhibited clear malicious behavior was 16.9% — a baseline rate for account takeover (ATO) attempts driven primarily by brute-force techniques like credential stuffing and password spraying.
cards.comparison: median across all Auth0 customers in 2024
cards.pageOrSection: Account takeovers (ATOs) present a constant threat

cards.title: Daily login-attack rate swung from 7.6% to 47.4%
cards.description: The 16.9% median masked dramatic day-to-day variability: across all of 2024, the highest daily rate of login attacks was 47.4% and the lowest 7.6%, including sustained multi-week ATO campaigns.
cards.comparison: min vs. max daily rate in 2024
cards.pageOrSection: Account takeovers (ATOs) present a constant threat

cards.title: Retail/eCommerce sees double the ATO attempts of the average industry
cards.description: Median daily proportion of login attempts meeting attack criteria in 2024, by industry. Retail/eCommerce was a clear outlier at 22.2%, with Professional Services and Financial Services hovering close to the all-industries mean of 10.0%.
cards.pageOrSection: Where suspected ATO attacks are concentrated

cards.title: Enterprises see the highest rate of malicious logins
cards.description: Median daily proportion of login attempts that met the criteria of a login attack in 2024, by customer segment. Enterprises endured the highest rate at 24.9%, while mid-market and small businesses faced ATO pressure at 7.6% and 9.4% respectively.
cards.pageOrSection: Account takeovers — by segment

cards.title: MFA abuse continues a multi-year decline
cards.description: Mean proportion of MFA events on the Auth0 platform classified as malicious. Falling from 12.7% in H1 2023 to a 2024 mean of 7.8% — and under 7% in the second half of 2024 — reflects improving secondary factors and tougher controls against MFA-fatigue and SMS-pumping attacks.
cards.pageOrSection: MFA abuse remains common, but may be declining

cards.title: 7.3%: median rate of malicious MFA events in 2024
cards.description: In 2024, the median daily proportion of MFA events detected as being malicious on the Auth0 platform was 7.3% — with the majority attributable to MFA-fatigue attacks and SMS pumping (toll fraud). The sparkline approximates the multi-year trajectory of malicious-MFA share.
cards.pageOrSection: MFA abuse remains common, but may be declining

cards.title: Media leads industries in malicious MFA events
cards.description: Median daily proportion of MFA events meeting the criteria of malicious activity in 2024, by industry. Media topped the chart at >20%, followed by Professional Services (17.6%) and Manufacturing (8.2%) — all well above the all-industries mean of 6.0%.
cards.pageOrSection: Lights, camera, attack: Media leads in malicious MFA events

cards.title: 11.6% of enterprise MFA events were malicious
cards.description: Enterprises experienced the highest proportion of malicious MFA events of any customer segment in 2024 — 11.6%, nearly double the overall 6.0% average. Mid-market organizations recorded the lowest abuse rate at 3.1%.
cards.pageOrSection: MFA by segment

cards.title: 68% of consumers admit to reusing passwords
cards.description: Despite years of warnings, 68% of users reported either using the same password for every account (17%) or reusing only a small set of passwords (51%) — poor hygiene that directly fuels credential-stuffing and ATO campaigns. 53% blame the inability to remember unique passwords.
cards.pageOrSection: More than two-thirds of respondents reuse passwords

cards.title: 64% of consumers are concerned about identity fraud
cards.description: Across the entire 6,750-respondent survey, 64% of users said they are concerned about identity fraud (32% very concerned, 32% concerned), while only 10% expressed little or no concern. Respondents from India were the most concerned (81% concerned or very concerned).
cards.pageOrSection: Identity fraud is a top-of-mind issue

cards.title: Banks earn the most trust to secure consumer data
cards.description: Consumers were asked how much they trust different sectors to secure their personal data. 63% trust banks and financial institutions; at the bottom, only 29% trust social-media platforms with the same. This trust gap shapes signup, login, and identity-sharing decisions.
cards.pageOrSection: With identity fraud emerging as a top concern…

cards.title: Nearly 1 in 4 shoppers abandon purchases due to signup or login friction
cards.description: 23% of respondents report either always (6%) or often (17%) abandoning an online purchase due to issues with signup or login processes; a further 40% report sometimes doing so. Tech Innovators are even more intolerant — 43% always or often abandon when faced with friction.
cards.pageOrSection: Signup and login issues drive customers away

cards.title: 62% say long signup or login forms are their top frustration
cards.description: Having to fill out long signup or login forms stands alone as the most frequently cited source of signup or login frustration — selected by 62% of respondents, well ahead of needing to provide private or sensitive information (52%).
cards.pageOrSection: Long forms are the most frustrating signup or login hurdle

cards.title: 73% of users still rate passwords as 'convenient'
cards.description: Despite the security weaknesses, 73% of respondents rated passwords as either very convenient (40%) or convenient (33%) — a full 10 percentage points above the second-most-convenient authentication method. The correlation between usage and perceived convenience was 0.92.
cards.pageOrSection: Convenience and familiarity drive login habits

cards.title: Biometrics dominate perceived security; social login lags
cards.description: Share of respondents who rated each authentication method as 'very secure' or 'secure'. Fingerprint (71%) and FaceID (62%) topped the rankings, while only 35% considered social login secure — a flag for marketers nudging users toward social SSO.
cards.pageOrSection: Customers point to fingerprints as the most secure

cards.title: 37% of consumers encounter AI agents very frequently or frequently
cards.description: Auth0's survey found that 37% of customers encounter AI agents on online platforms or websites either very frequently or frequently — a fast-rising baseline as GenAI-powered non-human identities (NHIs) begin acting on behalf of users.
cards.pageOrSection: AI meets customer identity

cards.title: Users prefer humans over AI agents by a 4.4-to-1 ratio
cards.description: Across the global survey, 70% favored interacting with humans while only 16% favored AI agents — a 4.4:1 ratio. Every cohort preferred humans; Tech Innovators were the closest (1.1) while Baby Boomers preferred humans by a striking 41.5-to-1.
cards.pageOrSection: Humans aren't sold on AI agents — yet

cards.title: 60% of consumers worry about AI's impact on identity privacy
cards.description: 60% of survey respondents reported being either very concerned or concerned about AI's impact on the privacy and security of their digital identities; only 9% were not concerned. Privacy fears are the top reason cited by non-adopters of AI agents (44%).
cards.pageOrSection: Privacy concern: AI's impact on identity

cards.title: 23% of consumers refuse to use AI agents at all
cards.description: 23% of respondents exclusively selected 'I would not use AI agents' — a stance driven largely by Tech Avoiders (73%), Baby Boomers (42%), Tech Traditionalists (43%) and respondents from Japan (37%). The leading reason (44%) is distrust of AI agents with personal information.
cards.pageOrSection: Hesitancy and AI agents

cards.title: The benefits of AI agents require trust above all
cards.description: Auth0's authors frame the report's central thesis: that as autonomous GenAI agents take on more user-facing tasks, customer identity and access management becomes the control plane for the trust those agents must earn.
cards.quote: "The benefits of AI agents are vast, but their actions require sensitive, valuable, and possibly even confidential information from businesses and consumers. Above all, their actions require trust."
cards.pageOrSection: AI meets customer identity
